caveat: Recycling acceptance depends on your local collection scheme, the item's design and how clean it is. Always check your local council or recycler's guidance.

materials.description: A clear, light and strong polyester. It keeps gases and moisture out well, which is why most drinks bottles are made from it.
properties: Good barrier to gas and moisture
Softens at around 70 °C, so not for hot filling or reheating
other_materials: Caps are usually PP or HDPE
Sleeves and labels are often PP, PET-G or paper
recycling_guidance: Empty and give a quick rinse
Squash to save space if your scheme allows
Follow local advice on whether to keep the cap on
Coloured and opaque PET is harder to recycle than clear PET
materials.recyclability_note: Bottles are among the most widely collected plastics. Trays and thermoformed packaging are accepted less often.
materials.fact: Recycled PET bottles are commonly turned into polyester fleece, carpet fibre and new bottles (rPET).
materials.eco_tip: A refillable bottle replaces hundreds of single-use PET bottles a year.
sources: ASTM D7611 Standard Practice for Coding Plastic Manufactured Articles for Resin Identification

materials.description: A stiff, tough polyethylene that resists many chemicals. It is usually opaque or milky, and is used for bottles that hold milk, detergent and cleaning products.
properties: Resists many acids, alkalis and detergents
other_materials: Labels may be paper or plastic film
recycling_guidance: Empty fully and rinse out residues
Replace or remove the cap as your scheme advises
Containers that held hazardous chemicals may need a separate drop-off
materials.recyclability_note: Bottles and jugs are widely collected. Large rigid items such as pipes and crates usually go to specialist recyclers.
materials.fact: Recycled HDPE is made into pipes, garden furniture, plastic lumber and new non-food bottles.
materials.eco_tip: Refill stations for detergent and shampoo let you reuse the same HDPE bottle many times.

materials.description: A durable plastic that contains chlorine. It is rigid on its own and is made flexible by adding plasticisers. Most PVC goes into building products rather than packaging.
common_items: Vinyl flooring and some cling films
other_materials: Plasticisers and stabilisers are often added
Blister packs are frequently bonded to card
recycling_guidance: Construction PVC (pipes, window frames) can often go to specialist take-back schemes
materials.recyclability_note: Household PVC packaging is seldom recycled, and a small amount of PVC can contaminate a batch of PET.
materials.fact: Burning PVC releases hydrogen chloride gas and can form dioxins, which is why open burning of plastic waste is so harmful.
materials.eco_tip: Choose packaging without PVC blisters where you can, and pass old pipes and frames to a builders' recycling scheme.

materials.description: A soft, flexible and stretchy polyethylene. It is used mainly for films and bags, as well as squeezable bottles.
other_materials: Often printed or laminated with other films
Cartons combine LDPE with paperboard and aluminium
recycling_guidance: Often not accepted in kerbside bins, because films tangle sorting machines
Many supermarkets run drop-off points for clean, dry films
Do the stretch test: films that stretch are usually polyethylene
materials.recyclability_note: Films can be recycled when collected separately and kept clean. Multi-layer and food-soiled films usually cannot.
materials.fact: Collected LDPE film is recycled into bin bags, composite decking and new film.
materials.eco_tip: Keep a reusable bag with you, and reuse bread and produce bags before dropping them off.

materials.description: A tough plastic that withstands heat (it melts at about 160 °C). That makes it the usual choice for containers that are microwaved or washed in hot water.
properties: Fatigue-resistant, so it can flex many times
other_materials: Lids may be a different plastic or aluminium foil
recycling_guidance: Increasingly accepted in kerbside collections. Check yours
Remove foil lids and recycle them separately where possible
materials.recyclability_note: Rigid tubs and pots are collected more and more often. Film and black PP are frequently rejected.
materials.fact: The thin flexible hinge on flip-top caps is called a living hinge. It works because PP can bend millions of times without breaking.
materials.eco_tip: Sturdy PP takeaway boxes make good reusable lunch and storage containers.

materials.description: Comes as a clear, brittle solid or as lightweight expanded foam (EPS). It is used for disposable cups, cutlery and protective packaging.
other_materials: Foam packaging may be combined with cardboard
recycling_guidance: Some recycling centres take clean EPS packaging foam
Keep foam out of the PET and PP bins
materials.recyclability_note: Expanded polystyrene is mostly air, so it is costly to transport and seldom recycled. Solid PS is recycled in only a few places.
materials.fact: Expanded polystyrene foam is about 95–98 % air by volume.
materials.eco_tip: Bring your own cup or container to cafés and takeaways that allow it.
